claims.text: The as-cast (TaNb)HfZrTi alloy is superconducting at ambient pressure.
Ambient-pressure electrical resistance and magnetic susceptibility provide a superconducting baseline for comparison.
Hydrostatic pressure compresses the alloy lattice and reduces its volume or lattice constant.
Pressure-induced lattice compression modifies the alloy's electronic band structure.
Lattice compression increases the density of states at the Fermi level.
An increased density of states at the Fermi level enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling improves Cooper pairing and raises Tc.
Tc initially increases with pressure relative to its ambient-pressure value.
Tc reaches a maximum at an intermediate optimal pressure below approximately 200 GPa.
Further compression beyond the optimal pressure reduces Tc.
The complete pressure dependence of Tc is non-monotonic, consisting of an increase, a maximum, and a subsequent decrease.
Over-compression degrades the beneficial electron-phonon coupling.
The proposed mechanism should remain applicable from ambient pressure to approximately 200 GPa in the absence of a structural transition.
The alloy retains its bcc structure without a structural phase transition to approximately 96 GPa.
Structural phase transitions or material degradation may occur above approximately 200 GPa.
Minute compositional and microstructural variations may affect the pressure and magnitude of the maximum Tc.

contradictions.description: The query requests an alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, but the selected alloy is presented as already superconducting and the cited evidence reports ambient-pressure zero resistance, diamagnetism, and pressure-dependent Tc.
